match.reason: None of the bank points teaches how human activities pollute water; they cover scarcity, managing supply, competing uses, green and blue water, and the forms of water, so the water quality idea needs a new point.

draft.title: How people affect water quality
card: Water quality is how clean and safe water is. A pollutant is a harmful substance or material that makes water dirtier or less safe.
Farm runoff
Rain washes fertiliser, animal waste and chemicals off paddocks into rivers. Extra nutrients can make algae grow fast and use up the oxygen that fish need.
Sewage and industrial waste
Sewage that is not treated well can carry germs into water. Factories can release chemicals and heavy metals if their waste is not controlled.
Rubbish and stormwater
Stormwater is rain that runs off roads and roofs into drains. It often flows to creeks and the sea without treatment, carrying litter, oil and dirt with it.
draft.remember: People's activities put pollutants in water, and rain and drains often carry them to rivers, lakes and the sea.

a.q: After heavy rain, fertiliser from a farm paddock washes into a nearby creek. What is this an example of?
opts: Farm runoff carrying a pollutant into a waterway
Sewage entering a river from a treatment plant
Stormwater washing litter off a city road
Industrial waste released from a factory pipe
a.why: Rain washed fertiliser off farmland and into a creek, which is farm runoff. Stormwater is similar because rain carries material into waterways, but it comes from roads and roofs in built-up areas, not paddocks.
a.clue: Think about where the fertiliser came from.

b.q: A storm hits a town in NSW. Rain runs off the streets, picks up litter and oil, and flows through drains into the nearby river. Which term best describes how the pollutants reached the river?
opts: Stormwater carried them through the drains
Farm runoff carried them from the paddocks
Sewage leaked into the river from homes
Industrial waste was poured in by a factory
b.why: The rain ran off streets and drains took it to the river, so this is stormwater. Farm runoff is the tempting choice because rain also carries pollutants, but this water came from a town's streets, not farmland.
b.clue: Where did the rain run off from, and what carried it to the river?

a.best: Farm runoff carrying a pollutant into a waterway

b.best: Stormwater carried them through the drains

proposal.title: How people affect water quality
card: Water quality is how clean and safe water is. A pollutant is a harmful substance or material that makes water dirtier or less safe.

proposal.remember: People's activities put pollutants in water, and rain and drains often carry them to rivers, lakes and the sea.

a.q: After heavy rain, fertiliser spread on a wheat crop washes into a nearby creek. What is this an example of?
a.why: Rain washed fertiliser off land used to grow crops and into a creek, which is farm runoff. Stormwater is the tempting choice because rain also carries material into waterways, but stormwater runs off roads and roofs in built-up areas, not crop land.
a.clue: Think about what kind of land the fertiliser was on.

b.q: In a NSW town, heavy rain runs off the streets and roofs, picks up litter and oil, and flows untreated into a nearby river. Which source of pollution is this?
b.why: Rain running off streets and roofs and flowing untreated to a river is stormwater. Farm runoff is the tempting choice because rain carries pollutants there too, but farm runoff comes off paddocks, not a town's streets and roofs.
b.clue: Where did the rain run off from?
